# Results — Study 870 (Industry-Leader Lead-Lag)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Hou
(2007): information diffuses **within an industry** from the biggest name outward, so the
**largest-cap** firm's return this week predicts its **followers'** return next week; long
the followers whose leader rose, short those whose leader fell. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close). Sample as-of 2026-06-30.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name → **861** weekly (W-FRI) returns |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Sectors / leaders | 8 GICS-style sectors (`SECTORS`); the **largest-cap** member of each is the leader (`LEADERS` = AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN, WMT, JPM, JNJ, XOM, GE) — a **static** public-record designation |
| Signal | for each sector: the **leader's week-`w` simple return**, known at that Friday's close, predicting the **followers' mean week-`w+1` return** |
| Book | long the sector's followers when the leader rose, short when it fell; weekly spread = `mean_s sign(leader_w) · mean_followers(ret_{w+1})` (equal per sector) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: leader through the close of week `w` → hold followers week `w+1`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per week on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the weekly spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled follower returns after up- vs down-leader weeks; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a two-era cut; a dollar-volume leader re-designation; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship & leader designation — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a
**current-membership** list of names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so magnitudes are
an **upper bound**. `LEADERS` inherits the same caveat: it is *today's* largest-cap per
sector, held static across the sample (Hou's "big firm"). Re-designating leaders by
trailing dollar volume (a size proxy read off the tape) leaves the verdict unchanged (below).

## The headline — long followers of up-leaders / short followers of down-leaders

Weekly equal-per-sector lead-lag spread (n = **859** weeks):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long up-leader followers − short down-leader followers)** | **−3.64 bps/week** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* | **−0.77** |
| one-sample *t* | −0.69 |
| followers after up-leader / after down-leader | +28.79 bps / +35.99 bps (Welch *t* = −1.99) |
| gross weekly Sharpe (no cost) | −0.17 |

The claimed edge **fails to replicate.** Hou predicts a *positive* spread (a leader's rise
foreshadows its followers' rise). On this liquid mega-cap tape the spread is a **statistically
indistinguishable −3.64 bps/week** (NW *t* = −0.77): the leader→follower diffusion channel is
**absent**. If anything the point estimate leans the *wrong* way — followers earned slightly
*more* after their leader *fell* (a whiff of reversal, Welch *t* = −1.99, not the diffusion
claimed). Slow within-industry information diffusion is a documented **small-and-illiquid-firm**
phenomenon; 50 mega-caps price sector news near-simultaneously, so there is no lag to harvest.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) spread a lucky lead→lag alignment?

Keep the sector structure but **shuffle the week-to-week alignment** of each leader's sign
against the followers' next-week return (the lead→lag link broken), 1,000 permutations
(20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−3.64 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +3.465 bps (4.935) |
| right-tail p (observed ≥ null) | **0.928** |

The permutation null sits *above* the observed value; the real spread is unremarkable
(p = 0.93). There is nothing in the true lead→lag alignment that a shuffled one lacks.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=415) | −13.96 bps | **−2.16** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=443) | +5.96 bps | +0.89 |

The sign **flips** across halves — significantly *negative* early, positive-insignificant
late. A signal that changes direction era-to-era and clears |t|≥2 only in the *wrong*
direction is the opposite of the robust positive the claim needs. Not one stable effect.

## Robustness — re-designate leaders by trailing dollar volume (size proxy)

Replace the static market-cap `LEADERS` with the largest-median-dollar-volume name per
sector (AAPL, META, AMZN, WMT, BAC, JNJ, XOM, BA): spread **−3.87 bps/week** (NW *t* =
−0.81, n = 859). Same non-result — the verdict does not hinge on the exact leader.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per week on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/wk | cost/wk | net/wk | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −3.64 bps | 2.96 bps | **−6.60 bps** | −1.24 | −0.31 | −3.4%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −3.64 bps | 10.96 bps | **−14.60 bps** | −2.75 | −0.68 | −7.6%/yr |

The specified book loses money gross, and the weekly round-trip friction only deepens the
hole. Even the sign-flipped book (+3.64 bps/week gross) is eaten whole by the 2.96 bps/week
cost at a mere 1 bp one-way. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel: each sector's leader carries a weekly latent shock that — with
`edge>0` — diffuses into its followers **one week later**. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.04** (sd 0.79), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.6`, seed 870) | **+20.79** (Welch *t* = +17.91) |

The detector recovers a *planted* leader→follower diffusion emphatically and never fires on
the null — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine absence of the effect, not a broken
sort. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The famous industry-leader lead-lag does **not** replicate on 50 liquid
  US mega-caps. The specified long-up-leader / short-down-leader followers spread is
  **−3.64 bps/week** (NW *t* = **−0.77**) — statistically indistinguishable from zero, on the
  *wrong* side if anything (followers drifted up more after a *down* leader; Welch *t* = −1.99),
  unremarkable against a 1,000-permutation placebo (p = 0.93), sign-flipping across eras
  (−13.96 / +5.96 bps), and unchanged when leaders are re-designated by dollar volume. A clean
  20-seed synthetic control recovers a *planted* diffusion (*t* = +20.79, fires on **0/20**
  nulls), so this is a true absence, not machinery. Slow diffusion is a small-illiquid-firm
  effect; mega-caps have no lag to harvest.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The specified book loses money gross and net (**−6.60 bps/week** at
  1 bp one-way, −14.60 at 5 bps); even the data-mined sign-flip is eaten by the weekly friction.
